title: Browser Agents Don't Need Better Models. They Need Better Eyes. - Kushan Raj, Sarvam AI
talk_summary: Kushan Raj argues browser agents fail not because of weak models but because of poor environment representation, and demonstrates a compressed markdown page representation plus change/feedback signals that lets a cheap model complete tasks in seconds where Claude got stuck for minutes. The core mechanism is token-efficient state representation with explicit diff and failure feedback rather than raw DOM or screenshots.

takeaways.what_they_do: Convert the full page into a compact markdown representation (~1,800 tokens) instead of raw DOM (~20,000 tokens) or a single screenshot (~1,100 tokens), so the agent sees the whole page cheaply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The full DOM for this would be around 20,000 tokens... My markdown's about 1,800 tokens
takeaways.numbers: DOM ~20,000 tokens vs markdown ~1,800 tokens vs screenshot ~1,100 tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: Tell the agent what newly appeared, what disappeared, and why a click failed, by tracking end-to-end page state across steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we say that okay, hey, these are the new things that have popped up on the page. This is now gone

takeaways.technique: Cheap model + better environment beats expensive model
takeaways.what_they_do: Same task completed faster with a much cheaper model once the environment representation was fixed, versus Claude stalling for minutes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm using a much cheaper model, right? The hypothesis here is models are pretty smart, but it's the infra around them that sucks
takeaways.numbers: Claude stuck ~2 minutes vs cheap-model run completing in seconds

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness reports that an attempted action did not take effect and why, rather than letting the model guess from a fresh screenshot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we give it feedback that you tried to click this, but that didn't happen because you know, we're keeping track
